note: All debut-volume manga (no light novels) that released last month and this month per otakucalendar.com, ranked against your collection. Covers link to Barnes & Noble.

items.t: Girls' Last Tour Collector's Edition: 1st Ration Pack
items.why: Tsukumizu's quiet, melancholy drifting is the same wavelength as March Comes in Like a Lion — and the 480-page deluxe HC is the version worth shelving.

items.t: Clevatess: The King of Dark Beasts, the Baby, and the Undead Hero, Vol. 1
items.why: Yuji Iwahara draws grime and monster design like Dorohedoro's cousin; this is the artsy-seinen action debut of the window.

items.t: What Does the Fox Say?, Vol. 1
items.meta: Aug 25 · Yen Press · yuri / office GL
items.why: The landmark Korean GL workplace drama finally in print — the biggest yuri debut in this window by a wide margin.
Masaaki Nakayama's Fuan no Tane is pure creeping dread with no explanation — exactly the register The Summer Hikaru Died works in.
A battery love triangle — two catchers, one pitcher. Sports manga structure carrying the BL, which is how you judge the genre.
Deep-sea creature rescue with real craft in the environmental art — the quiet-obsessive-profession lane you keep buying into.
Masamune Shirow's foundational cyberpunk in a proper hardcover — a shelf anchor, not a casual read.
Io Sakisaka (Ao Haru Ride) is the strongest cartoonist launching a romance this window; VIZ is putting weight behind it.
Young Magazine superhero deconstruction that already has a confirmed 11-volume ending — a contained commitment.

items.t: Hand in Hand with Mu-chan: Lessons from My Autistic Daughter, Vol. 1
items.meta: Aug 25 · Yen Press · autobiographical essay manga
items.why: Nonfiction slice-of-life with real stakes; the contemplative lane next to Blue Period rather than the plot-driven one.
VIZ Jump romcom about killing time together — low-stakes hangout energy, Days on Fes adjacent.

items.t: You Might As Well Be the One, Vol. 1
items.why: College-age romance about being misread by everyone; more grounded than the usual shojo debut.
Fresh Yen license in the teasing-romcom mold — pleasant, not essential.
Stylish assassin thriller; worth a flip-through if the art grabs you the way Dorohedoro's did.

items.t: Castle in the Sky Film Comic: All-in-One Edition
items.why: Keepsake more than a read — the complete Laputa film comic in one volume for the first time.

items.meta: Jul 21 · Ize Press · BL manhwa (full color)
items.why: Full-color print of a well-reviewed BL webtoon; the story holds up on its own, which is your bar for the genre.
Umi Ruike debut with an appealing hook, but nothing yet says it clears your shelf bar.

items.t: Elden Ring: Distant Tales Between, Vol. 1
items.meta: Aug 25 · Yen Press · game tie-in fantasy
items.why: Side-story anthology from the Lands Between — only if the game means something to you.
Cozy monster-vet procedural; charming, but a lighter read than most of what you keep.
Sequel-series debut for a huge franchise — fine action, but not the kind of book you shelve.

items.t: The Bubble Love of the Mermaid, Vol. 1 (manga)
items.why: Manga adaptation of an Agitogi novel; pretty, but adaptation-of-a-novel is usually your skip signal.

items.meta: Aug 4 · Square Enix (Manga UP!) · gender-swap romcom
items.why: Isekai-adjacent fantasy romcom — squarely outside the lane you actually read.
